You Have Less Than 10 Days To Use The Best AI Ever Made

 Claude Fable 5 Is Here: The Mythos-Class AI That Beat Pokemon, Topped Coding Benchmarks, and Sparked a Pricing Debate 🤖✨

 🚀 The Big Release Everyone Is Talking About

The AI world has a new heavyweight. Claude Fable 5 just dropped, and it is being described as a Mythos-class model meaning it carries the raw capabilities of the powerful Mythos 5, but wrapped in safety restrictions around cybersecurity and biological knowledge. 🛡️ Think of it as the public-facing, safer sibling of one of the most capable AI systems ever built.

So what does that actually mean for developers, businesses, and everyday users? Quite a lot, as it turns out. 👀

 📊 Performance: State-of-the-Art Across the Board

Claude Fable 5 is posting state-of-the-art numbers in software engineering, knowledge work, and vision tasks. But the real story is what happens when tasks get long and complicated. The harder and longer the task, the bigger the gap between Fable 5 and everything else. 📈

On the coding side, it now leads both SweetBench Pro and Frontier Code two of the most respected coding benchmarks in the industry. 🥇 For developers, this is not a small bump. This is leadership territory. 💪

 💰 The Price Tag That Made People Gasp

Here is where the excitement cools down a bit. 😬 API pricing sits at 10 dollars per million input tokens and 50 dollars per million output tokens. That is steep really steep especially for hobby projects or casual experimentation. 💸

There is also a clear shift happening: less generous access through subscriptions, and a stronger push toward usage-based billing. The message is simple: if you want frontier intelligence, you will increasingly pay frontier prices. To justify daily use, your work needs to generate real value. ⚠️

 ⏰ Availability: Use It Before June 23

Right now, Claude Fable 5 is included in Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans but only temporarily. ⌛ After June 23, access will require usage credits, with a possible future restoration depending on infrastructure capacity.

Translation: if you want to try the model without extra cost, the clock is ticking. ⏳

 🎮 It Beat Pokemon. Autonomously. The Whole Game. 🔥

This is the demo that lit social media on fire. Claude Fable 5 completed the entire Pokemon Fire Red game on its own, using nothing but screenshots as input. 📸 No shortcuts, no hand-holding just persistent, long-horizon decision making from start to finish. 🏆

It also handled Slay the Spire, a far more strategically demanding game that requires planning, adaptation, and real-time decision making. 🃏

Why does gaming matter? Because games are a surprisingly honest measure of intelligence: they test planning, adaptation, and the ability to actually finish a goal. 🎯 Beating a full game autonomously is not a party trick it is a milestone. 🏁

 💬 The Community Is Genuinely Impressed

Reception has been overwhelmingly positive, and not just from hype accounts. 🙌 Experienced developers are calling this a meaningful capability jump.

The most notable endorsement came from antirez, the legendary creator of Redis, who said working with Fable 5 feels like discussing code with an expert programmer. 🧠 He highlighted its improved reasoning on niche and underrepresented codebases exactly the kind of work where most AI models fall apart. He even suggested this could be a step toward genuinely automatic programming. 🤯

 🏖️ Real-World Test: Building an Actual Website

In hands-on testing, the model built a beach house management website organizing information, generating restaurant recommendations with working external links 🔗, and adding review functionality ⭐. The layouts were attractive, the user interface was clean, and it even handled SEO improvements and content restructuring without breaking a sweat. 😎

 ✅ Strengths and Weaknesses at a Glance

What it does brilliantly: 💚 high-quality code generation, strong reasoning, polished web design output, long task completion, autonomous problem solving, and complex workflow execution.

Where it stumbles: ❌ it is expensive, responses are slower 🐢, and for everyday work it feels incremental rather than revolutionary. The cost-benefit math will not work for everyone. 🧮

 🏢 The Bigger Picture: AI Is Getting Expensive

Fable 5 reflects a wider industry trend. 🌍 AI companies are chasing profitability, leaning into API-first access models, and quietly making the best models harder to reach. Premium intelligence is becoming a premium product. 💎

There is also a healthy debate brewing: gaming demos are visually stunning and easy to showcase, but professionals care about ROI career advancement, business productivity, real outcomes. 📊 Beating Pokemon is impressive. Paying the bills with it is another matter. 💵

 ⚖️ How It Stacks Up Against the Competition

OpenAI, Google, and DeepSeek all have strong contenders, and models like Opus 4.8 and GPT 5.5 Fast already deliver excellent results. 🥊 What sets Fable 5 apart is its reasoning depth and a noticeably higher capability ceiling especially on the hard stuff. 🧗

 🎯 The Verdict

Claude Fable 5 is a genuinely good model and a significant improvement worth testing but it is not life-changing, and the cost remains the biggest sticking point. 💭 It represents a meaningful step toward software engineering automation and long-horizon AI reasoning, without yet transforming professional workflows entirely.

Bottom line: if you have a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan, try it before the June 23 window closes. ⏰ Frontier AI is advancing fast and getting pricier just as quickly. 🚀💸

Fable 5 just turned me into an iOS developer.

I spent 2 days building a full game with zero code written by hand. 

The last 10 builds succeeded on the first try.

I needed a fun project to test it on, so I decided to make an iOS game. After a few experiments with other ideas, I settled on a runner starring Dario as the main character, called "Credit Runner". Hilarious, I know!

In terms of credits spent, my Claude Max plan stands at 36% right now, and this isn't the only project I ran through Fable 5.

A few quick notes:
- This is just an early prototype, a long way from release, but it's really fun to play!
- It's extremely fun to work with Fable 5!
- Fable 5 wants to get things done, and it pushes you towards completion much faster than any other model.
- Once we established the ground rules, how I wanted the game built, and the overall structure, the last 10 builds were flawless, succeeding on the first try. This is impressive!
- All the assets were generated with AI (Magnific and Trippo for the visuals, ElevenLabs for the voices). The only thing that's not AI is the music. I just really liked this track.
- There are many rules in the game designed to make it really fun to play, especially the randomness.
- There are a lot of visual cues inspired by San Francisco, and I hope you catch them all.
- At some point on the first day, I honestly thought I wasn't going to get where I wanted, but Fable pushed me towards the goal, and by the second day it started to deeply understand the project.
- The prompts were really long, especially in the beginning, to make sure everything was covered.
- Once the app was solid, I tried to pack as many changes as I could into a single prompt to maximize my Fable usage.

This was just a fun project, but if anyone wants to play it, I might put the final, much more polished version on the App Store.

What do you think? Should I?
